  *****NOTE FROM THE CITY*****

Doors to the City Council Chamber will open at 1:30 p.m. for Open Session. Please be mindful that
seating is limited and available on a first come, first served basis.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting
convenience:

  ¡  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.
  ¡  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video,
  at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

Inglewood, California
  March 26, 2024

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  March 26, 2024, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Parking
  Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:01 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Parking
  Authority/Joint Powers Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as
  follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Parking Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers
  Authority Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor
  Agency Members/Housing Authority Members/Parking
  Authority Members/ Joint Powers Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Parking Authority/ Joint Powers Authority
  officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Parking Authority,
  and Joint Powers Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Parking Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers
  Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address
  the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Parking Authority/Joint Powers
  Authority on any item on the Agendas.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke concerning parking permits and signs with two-hour
  restrictions in front of her residence. She complained about street parking and received
  four tickets with her parking permit displayed. Finally, the speaker complained about the
  height of the parking meters and recommended lowering them.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated March
  22, 2024, in the amount of $4,694,959.35, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor
  Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the Minutes for the City Council Meeting held on January 23, 2024, be
  approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.
 March 26, 2024

171  AMENDMENT NO. 3 TO AGREEMENT NO. 21-117 APPROVED – BATEMAN
  COMMUNITY LIVING, LLC DBA TRIO COMMUNITY MEALS. Staff report dated
  March 26, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members
  approve Amendment No. 3 to Agreement No. 21-117 with Bateman Community Living,
  LLC, dba TRIO Community Meals, extending the term of the agreement by one year to
  provide meals onsite for the Senior Nutrition Program, in an annual amount not to exceed
  $795,600 (total contract amount of $3,182,400).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 3 to Agreement No. 21-117. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171 & 183  BID NO. CB-23-22 REJECTED – VINCENT PARK PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT
  REPLACEMENT PROJECT. Staff report dated March 26, 2024, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members reject all bids received on November
  1, 2023, for the Vincent Park Playground Equipment Replacement Project (Bid No. CB-
  23-22).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject all bids; and 2) Authorize the rebidding of the
  project. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171 & 183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 24-163 APPROVED – GA
  BUILDERS, LLC, DBA GA CONSTRUCTION. Staff report dated March 26, 2024, was
  presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members award a contract and
  approve an agreement with GA Builders, LLC, dba GA Construction, for the Vincent Park
  Restroom Project Phase 3, per Bid No. CB-23-23.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Award contract and approve Agreement No. 24-163 in an
  amount not to exceed $678,000; and 2) Authorize an additional City-controlled and directed
  ten (10%) contingency in an amount not to exceed $67,800, for a total amount of $745,800.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171 & 183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 24-164 APPROVED –
  VOLTAIRE ENGINEERING, INC.; RESOLUTION NO. 24-42 ADOPTED -
  AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 OPERATING BUDGET. Staff report
  dated March 26, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members
  award a contract and approve an agreement with Voltaire Engineering, Inc., for the Vincent
  Park Soccer Field Parking Area Improvement Project, per Bid No. CB-23-28.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Award contract and approve Agreement No. 24-164 in the
  amount of $173,050 (with a contingency of $18,000, for a total amount of up to $191,050);
  and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 24-42 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 BUDGET TO
  APPROPRIATE $191,050 FOR THE VINCENT PARK SOCCER FIELD
  PARKING AREA IMPROVEMENT PROJECT (CB-23-28)

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
 March 26, 2024

178  CALIFORNIA BOARD OF STATE AND COMMUNITY CORRECTIONS
  OFFICER WELLNESS AND MENTAL HEALTH GRANT FUNDS ACCEPTED;
  RESOLUTION NO. 24-43 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE 2023-2024 FISCAL YEAR
  OPERATING BUDGET. Staff report dated March 26, 2024, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members accept the California Board of State

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA ACCEPTING GRANT FUNDS FROM THE BOARD OF STATE
  AND COMMUNITY CORRECTIONS IN THE AMOUNT OF $120,056.14 AND
  AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 OPERATING BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

103.3  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 24-165 APPROVED – S&L
  SPECIALTY CONSTRUCTION, INC. (S&L); RESOLUTION NO. 24-44 ADOPTED
  - AMENDING THE 2023-2024 FISCAL YEAR OPERATING BUDGET. Staff report
  dated March 26, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members
  award a contract and approve an agreement with S&L Specialty Construction, Inc. (S&L),
  to provide residential sound insulation work on 76 residential units (RSI Phase XV, Group
  40).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Award contract and approve Agreement No. 24-165 in an
  amount not to exceed $1,215,900; 2) Approve a City-controlled and directed 10%
  contingency of $121,590, and a special expense of $25,460, per Bid No. CB-24-05; and 3)
  Adopt Resolution No. 24-44 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2023/2024 ANNUAL BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  RESOLUTION NO. 24-45 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024
  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM (CIP) BUDGET. Staff report dated March
  26, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members adopt a
  resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Capital Improvement Program (CIP)
  Budget to appropriate $8,661,611.23 in funding for Agreement No. 23-046 with Ferreira
  Coastal Construction Co. for the Los Angeles World Airports (LAWA) Intelligent
  Transportation Systems (ITS) Project.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that Resolution
  No. 24-45 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 BUDGET TO
  APPROPRIATE $8,661,611.23 IN FUNDING FOR AGREEMENT NO. 23-046
  WITH FERREIRA COSTAL CONSTRUCTION CO.

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  3
 March 26, 2024

183  ENCROACHMENT PERMIT NO. 24-166 APPROVED – PROPOSED
  APARTMENT BUILDING AT 939 W. MANCHESTER BOULEVARD,
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA. Staff report dated March 26, 2024, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members approve the Public Works Director
  Encroachment Permit for the proposed apartment building at 939 W. Manchester
  Boulevard, Inglewood, California.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby approve Encroachment Permit No. 24-166. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

126  MONTHLY TREASURER’S REPORT. Staff report dated March 26, 2024, was
  presented submitting the Monthly Treasurer’s Report for the Month ending February 29,
  2024.

  Mayor Butts ordered the report received and filed.

126  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson congratulated
  Councilwoman Gray on her Town Hall Meeting held on March 25, 2024. She stated that it
  was well attended and that it was great to see Congresswoman Maxine Waters there to
  speak with the residents. The City Clerk also stated that it was a pleasure to be there with
  everyone. Finally, she wished Angela Allen, Deputy City Clerk, a happy birthday.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke concerning the former City Clerk, Yvonne Horton, in
  2015 when the speaker was homeless. She stated there seemed to be a disagreement  about
  determining if the City had the right to eminent domain and that she is debating it with
  Congresswoman Maxine Waters in Compton. The speaker mentioned attending a Legacy
  Meeting with NHS in Compton and writing to their corporate office. She also  mentioned that
  her spiritual intent was to regularly participate in the City Council Meetings if it didn’t conflict
  with Compton’s City Hall Meetings, starting at 5:30 p.m. The  speaker  discussed  the
  misappropriation of funds from the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, and she gave her
  word to Congresswoman Water and a  Supervisor to get all of Compton’s money back.
  Finally, she noted that she wasn’t sure if  the appropriated funds would be transferred to
  Inglewood because many people are no  longer in business.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts welcomed Council Member
  Gray’s grandson and declared the meeting adjourned at the hour of 2:30 p.m.

  Approved this 30th day of April, 2024.
  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
